- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥15 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- When true outcome shows “rebound” after dip (e.g., 50→53), model often misses it; add 1–2% buffer for next 3–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ positive signals, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when recent history includes 3+ consecutive spikes; apply “spike correction” by +2–5% for next 3 days.
- If forecast is >10% below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model is lagging; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term sentiment; ignore sentiment if >10% of recent 18-day history is negative.
